Bench Press Guide

Learn how to bench press with cleaner form, avoid common mistakes, progress your sets, and track bench press workouts in LogWise.

TRACK THIS LIFT IN LOGWISE → CALCULATE YOUR 1RM →
ChestWORKING SETSRIR
QUICK FACTS
Primary muscles
Chest, front delts, triceps
Equipment
Barbell, flat bench, rack
Movement pattern
Horizontal press
Best for
Upper-body strength and pressing volume
FORM GUIDE

How to do the Bench Press

  1. Set your eyes under the bar, plant your feet, and pull your shoulder blades back into the bench.
  2. Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width and keep your wrists stacked over your elbows.
  3. Unrack with control, lower the bar toward the mid-to-lower chest, and keep the elbows slightly tucked.
  4. Touch the chest without bouncing, then press up and back until the bar is over the shoulders.
  5. Keep your hips on the bench and repeat each rep with the same setup and bar path.
COMMON MISTAKES

Keep the lift honest

  • Bouncing the bar off the chest instead of controlling the bottom.
  • Letting the shoulders roll forward before or during the press.
  • Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides on every rep.
  • Lifting the hips off the bench to turn the set into a different movement.
HOW TO PROGRESS

Make progress measurable

  • Add reps inside a fixed range before adding load, such as 3 sets of 6-8.
  • Use small load jumps on pressing movements when possible.
  • Track working-set volume so extra bench work does not quietly outpace recovery.
  • Leave 1-3 reps in reserve on most sets and save true grinders for planned tests.

Use the workout volume calculator when sets, reps, or load change enough that recovery becomes harder to judge.

TRACKING TIPS

What to log in LogWise

  • Log each set with weight, reps, and RIR so your next target is obvious.
  • Add notes for grip width, pause reps, shoulder comfort, or spotter help.
  • Use estimated 1RM as a trend, not as a reason to max out every week.

If you want a paper structure first, the workout log template captures the same basics: sets, reps, weight, RIR, and notes.

LogWise cues

  • Retract and lock shoulder blades into the bench before unracking.
  • Touch bar to mid-lower chest without bouncing.
  • Keep feet flat on floor; hips must stay on the bench.
  • Lower slowly (~2 sec), then press up powerfully.

Track the useful numbers

For this lift, the most useful history is simple: top set, back-off sets, total working volume, RIR, and short technique notes.
